summary: fill()'s new inner read loop reads until the buffer is full or EOF instead of returning after a usable line is available, regressing streaming/interactive/line-buffered latency (tail -f, journalctl -f).
Changed glue.rs golden byte-count constants (262146->262142) are undocumented magic numbers / unexplained --stats shift.
roll() comment 'skip this step when before_context==0' does not match the code (preceding() is called unconditionally).
Narrowing roll() lookback to before_context leaves correctness on an implicit, unguarded invariant (no debug_assert).
CHANGELOG links issue #3184 with a /pull/ URL though #3184 is the issue (PR is #3185).
LineBuffer ordering/bound invariants expressed only in prose over bare usize fields, not type-enforced.
Inner read loop propagates ErrorKind::Interrupted via ? instead of retrying (noted pre-existing).
In Quit binary mode the loop drains the buffer before binary detection, over-reading past a NUL by up to a buffer's worth.
CHANGELOG wording 'performance of large values with -A' reads awkwardly.
fill() inner loop's fill-to-capacity rationale not documented in code (only the commit message), so a maintainer could simplify it and reintroduce #3184.
EOF or error mid-accumulation inside the new inner loop is untested.
No regression test covers the roll() before_context-vs-max_context change across a buffer roll with large -A.
No test exercises fill()'s new multi-short-read amortization / incremental-read accumulation path.
self.last_lineterm = self.end has no explanatory comment.
Read result bound to readlen; every other manual read loop in the crate names it nread.
Inner loop advances self.end after each read, so a later read error in the same pass discards already-read bytes.
Binary detection spanning a read boundary is untested.
before/after/max_context() are three interchangeable bare usize (weak typing behind the regression).
